messages.subject: Error using a truncated Poisson
parts:
I am attempting to fit a truncated poisson model. Based on my understanding of the manual and previous posts, the truncation function should work with poisson as poisson has a cdf function. The model parses but then I get an error. I am using Stan 1.3.0, rstan 1.3.0, and R 3.0.1 -- Mac OS 10.8.5. I have attached a .csv file with the rapi data in it.

My outcome is a count that does not have any zero values and starts at 1. Thus, I would like to use a truncated poisson likelihood with a lower limit of 1 (I'm going to ultimately fit a more complicated model to deal with some of the complexity of the data but wanted to get a base model running).

My model is:

  data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int rapi[N]; // outcome variable;
  }
  parameters {
    real beta0; 
  }
  model {
    rapi ~ poisson(exp(beta0)) T[1, ];
  }

I get the following error during compilation:

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! file1690b7cb6b998.cpp: In member function ‘T__ model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan_namespace::model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan::log_prob_poly(std::vector<T, std::allocator<_T2> >&, std::vector<int, std::allocator<int> >&, std::ostream*)’:
file1690b7cb6b998.cpp:133: error: no match for ‘operator<’ in ‘((model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan_namespace::model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan*)this)->model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan_namespace::model1690b3f1e035_hurdle1_stan::rapi < 1’
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/rstan/include//stansrc/stan/agrad/rev/operator_less_than.hpp:40: note: candidates are: bool stan::agrad::operator<(double, const stan::agrad::var&)
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/rstan/include//stansrc/stan/agrad/rev/operator_less_than.hpp:28: note:                 bool stan::agrad::operator<(const stan::agrad::var&, double)
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions
In addition: Warning message:
running command '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R CMD SHLIB file1690b7cb6b998.cpp 2> file1690b7cb6b998.cpp.err.txt' had status 1

The model runs fine if I remove the T[1, ];

Any thoughts?

Additionally, will I achieve the same thing as truncation by changing the data portion of the stan code to:

  data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int<lower=1> rapi[N]; // outcome variable;
  }

and thus provide an explicit lower limit for the outcome variable. This would be nice because the poisson_log_log distribution doesn't accept truncation. However, it seems like the truncated poisson would be proportional to the full poisson so maybe none of this matters in Stan.

Thanks for your help.

Best,
Scott

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error using a truncated Poisson
parts:
The truncated distributions aren't vectorized yet.
If you do this:

for (n in 1:N)
rapi[n] ~ poisson(exp(beta0)) T[1, ];

it should work.

We didn't trap this error in 1.3. In 2.0, the output will be this:

|
--- Translating Stan graphical model to C++ code ---
bin/stanc ../temp2/baldwin.stan --o=../temp2/baldwin.cpp
Model name=baldwin_model
Input file=../temp2/baldwin.stan
Output file=../temp2/baldwin.cpp

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=../temp2/baldwin.stan; line=9, column=37

^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Outcomes in truncated distributions must be univariate.
Found outcome expression: rapi
with non-univariate type: int[1]
Parser expecting: <eps>
|

The messages should get a bit less confusing post-2.0, because
we're cleaning up error handling further. Right now, the "Parser expecting: <eps>"
is not something we should be exposing to users --- it's an artifact of my
limited understanding of the Boost parser's error handling mechanism.

- Bob
